page: Amazon Web Services g6f.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware foundation features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 64 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per virtual core ratio. Acceleration is powered by a partitioned NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU providing 11 GB of dedicated video memory. Local scratch capacity includes a bundled 450 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 10 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results highlight strong prompt processing throughput in machine learning inference tasks. Processing prompts on smaller 135M parameter models achieves 4312.41 tokens per second, while 7B parameter models reach 1062.16 tokens per second, placing the instance in the top tier for these workloads. Token generation registers moderate metrics, clocking 183.24 tokens per second on 135M models and 23.69 tokens per second on 7B models. Compute evaluation demonstrates high single-core capabilities with a stress-ng score of 2986.88, alongside balanced multi-core metrics including a Geekbench multi-core score of 9475.0 and PassMark CPU score of 22835.11.

A notable architectural limitation appears in large-block uncached memory bandwidth, which falls into the lower performance quartile at 38.61 GB/s read and 22.63 GB/s write. However, cached small-block operations demonstrate robust throughput at 1098.83 GB/s. For storage operations, the bundled 450 GB local NVMe SSD provides low-latency workspace for temporary files and local models, avoiding network storage latency.

From an operational cost perspective, the partitioned 0.5 NVIDIA L4 GPU configuration offers an efficient entry point for applications requiring graphics processing or tensor acceleration without bearing the expense of a dedicated full GPU. Amazon Web Services g6f.4xlarge is well fitted for real-time AI inference pipelines, video decoding, light graphics rendering, and machine learning development workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services g6f.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for graphics and artificial intelligence tasks. It features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, delivering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores, paired with 64 GB of DDR4 memory. Hardware acceleration is provided by a fractional NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU equipped with 11 GB of VRAM. Storage includes a integrated 450 GB local NVMe SSD alongside a 10 Gbps baseline network link. In synthetic and practical testing, the instance exhibits top-tier prompt processing speeds on small and mid-sized language models, alongside strong single-core CPU execution. System memory reveals lower uncached large-block throughput, but cached and multi-threaded decompression tests maintain solid mid-tier output. This hardware balance makes the configuration suitable for cost-conscious AI inference, remote workstation streaming, image processing, and media transcoding pipelines.
